Also left out: Krea 3 at Creative Boom and the Adobe 99U piece at It's Nice That (both sponsored), a member-only UX Collective essay on brand foundations with Claude, essays by Karri Saarinen and Andrew Boardman without a transferable core, Fulham FC and Otherwander identities (brand quota), Which? positioning release, Creative Bloq reviews and celebrity posters, and general TechCrunch, The Verge, Ars Technica and MIT Technology Review AI-industry news. stories.title: Collins builds Remote's identity on one rule: every cube converges on the same vanishing point
stories.blurb: The payroll platform's new system uses a stackable cube as a nod to infrastructure, drawn flat, in one-point perspective or isometric, plus a custom blocky wordmark and a palette taken from banknotes. The useful detail is the constraint: however many cubes appear, all perspective edges meet at one point, which keeps a flexible system reading as one.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: Collins centres Remote s new identity on banknote colours and building blocks

stories.title: Kiwibank's mascot escaped, and the takedown campaign made it worse
stories.blurb: After its AI-animated sheep Buck went viral for the wrong reasons, the bank filed copyright claims and turned a passing meme into a censorship story. The piece argues that audiences now treat popular mascots as remixable cultural property, and contrasts Kiwibank with McDonald's, which let the Grimace Shake trend run without intervening.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: The Kiwibank sheep went viral for all the wrong reasons, and there's something every brand can learn from it

stories.title: Audi Denmark turns billboards into road directions to the nearest blood donation centre
stories.blurb: Twenty's "Powered by Detour" swaps the ad message for navigation language, such as "Turn right in 250 metres and save up to three lives", with each site pointing to a real centre nearby in seven Danish cities. A clean example of a brand using its own territory, mobility, to shorten the gap between intent and action.

sources.name: Roastbrief
sources.headline: Audi and Twenty Turn Advertising Billboards into Directions That Could Save Lives

stories.title: If everyone researches on synthetic customers, real ones become the differentiator
stories.blurb: State of Brand collects how Kenvue, Goodway, WPP and others now test against simulated buyers, and notes that even vendors say the models drift toward the most common answer. Its argument: when competitors ask similar models similar questions, positioning converges, and named customers speaking on the record become the material no model can produce.

sources.name: State of Brand
sources.headline: Synthetic Customers Are Taking Over Market Research. It's the Best News Brand Storytellers Have Had in Years. | State of Brand

stories.title: Singapore's A4 paper signs show where an official wayfinding system stopped keeping up
stories.blurb: Station managers fill the MRT with self-made printouts next to the professional signage, and the author reads them as evidence that the network outgrew its system rather than as an aesthetic problem. Includes the history of the official redesigns since 2001, useful for anyone judging when a signage system needs rethinking instead of patching.

sources.name: It's Nice That
sources.headline: Design disasters or creative solutions? The self-made paper signs replacing wayfinding in Singapore’s railway stations

stories.title: Indie game developers stop showing early work because AI clones arrive before launch
stories.blurb: Alliance Arts pulled its Steam Next Fest demo into closed sessions, and Freya Holmér saw vibe-coded copies of a shared prototype within days. The same bind applies to any creative studio that markets through work in progress: showing builds the audience, and now also hands over the idea.

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.headline: AI game clones are making indie developers afraid to show their work

stories.title: Almost half of marketing teams replaced tasks with AI this year, few measure the payoff
stories.blurb: Basis surveyed 184 marketers: 47.8% replaced human tasks with AI, up from 27.9%, but only 6.5% measure the investment against benchmarks. Agents now draft campaign briefs in 56.4% of teams and create content in 45.7%, which State of Brand reads as the junior job description disappearing first.

sources.name: State of Brand
sources.headline: Half of Marketing Teams Are Replacing People With AI. Almost Nobody Can Prove It's Working | State of Brand
